item.text: {"search_note":"I found little solid 2024 evidence that Sisi expanded equal political standing for Copts, Nubians, or North Sinai residents specifically. The strongest positives were about women’s economic inclusion and refugee service access, not equal political power or protection for unpopular viewpoints. The independent reporting points the other way: refugees, dissenters, journalists, and LGBT+ people remained exposed to discrimination, coercion, and prosecution.","evidence":[{"title":"Women’s Empowerment Strategy 2030 was treated as a working state document","publisher":"State Information Service","date":"2024-03-12","url":"https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/strategies/womens-empowerment-strategy-2030/","summary":"Sisi assigned the strategy to the government and state agencies, and the page frames it as expanding women’s leadership and equal opportunity. This is a weak positive for women’s inclusion, but it is policy rhetoric, not proof of equal political power.","question_ids":["4B.7"]},{"title":"Labor ministry said women’s economic equality was being pursued under Sisi’s directives","publisher":"State Information Service","date":"2024-03-23","url":"https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/minister-labor-ministry-has-strategy-to-empower-women/","summary":"The ministry described training, job-placement, and a gender-equality unit at Sisi’s direction. This supports a limited inclusion claim, but it is still mainly economic and administrative.","question_ids":["4B.7"]},{"title":"UN agencies said Egypt had taken notable steps on refugee education, but many children were still out of school","publisher":"UNHCR Egypt","date":"2024-08-22","url":"https://www.unhcr.org/eg/news/education-cannot-wait-unhcr-unicef-strategic-partners-call-increased-resources","summary":"The joint UN statement says the government had taken notable steps to provide refugees access to education services, but roughly 54% of newly arrived children were out of school. That is a partial inclusion signal, not equal political treatment.","question_ids":["4B.7"]},{"title":"Sisi signed a new refugees law, but it was only a formal framework","publisher":"Human Rights Studies - Egypt / SIS","date":"2024-12-17","url":"https://hrightsstudies.sis.gov.eg/en/press/local/sisi-signs-foreign-refugees-law/","summary":"The state says the law created a formal refugee framework and committee. This is a weak positive on paper, but it does not show effective equal standing in practice.","question_ids":["4B.7"]},{"title":"Amnesty documented mass arrests and forced returns of Sudanese refugees","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-06-19","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/mde12/8101/2024/en/","summary":"Border forces and police arbitrarily arrested Sudanese refugees, held women, men, and children in cruel conditions, and forced returns without asylum access. This is strong evidence against equal protection for a vulnerable group.","question_ids":["4B.7","4B.4","4B.5","4B.6"]},{"title":"Amnesty said the new asylum law restricted rights and enabled abuse","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-12-03","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/12/egypt-president-al-sisi-must-reject-new-asylum-law-which-violates-refugee-rights/","summary":"Amnesty said the law undermined asylum rights, lacked due process, and included broad exclusions and movement restrictions. That cuts against political equality for refugees and other excluded groups.","question_ids":["4B.7","4B.4","4B.5"]},{"title":"Freedom House described Egypt as not free, with discrimination against women and LGBT+ people","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/egypt/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House says meaningful opposition is virtually nonexistent, liberties are tightly restricted, and discrimination against women and LGBT+ people remains serious. This is strong structural evidence against political equality.","question_ids":["4B.7","4B.5","4B.6"]},{"title":"HRW reported renewed prosecutions of critics and continued media curbs","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-08-29","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/29/egypt-spate-free-speech-prosecutions","summary":"HRW said authorities renewed prosecutions of critics, including satirist Ashraf Omar, and kept mainstream media severely curtailed. This is direct evidence against protection of unpopular viewpoints.","question_ids":["4B.7","4B.5","4B.6"]}]}
